**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

- **No exclusivity binds us.** There is no sole-supplier, requirements, or "shall not procure from any third party" obligation on Sanofi anywhere in the Agreement.
- **Exclusivity runs in our favour** — Section 3.1 grants Sanofi an exclusive licence (even as to RevMed) and an exclusive option; Section 13.2(q) is a RevMed warranty that no third-party exclusivity limits our rights. Per the detection guidance, these are not deviations.
- **Sourcing freedom preserved** — Article VII gives Sanofi oversight of Registrational/commercial Manufacture, obliges RevMed to transfer Manufacturing Know-How and to support Sanofi in setting up its *own* third-party supply agreements (7.2), and 7.3 is only a good-faith negotiation obligation where one Party actually manufactures for the other.
- **Noted, not flagged:** Section 12.2(d) lets RevMed terminate if Sanofi develops a Competing Product without having commenced a Registrational Clinical Trial, subject to a Sanofi cure election. That is a conditional termination right, not an exclusive-dealing covenant, and is standard for this collaboration structure — so it does not fail the fallback.
